chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you are in the obligatory salat (prayer) and you see a servant of yours who has run away, or a debtor of yours who has property owed, or a snake that you fear for yourself from, then break the salat (prayer), follow your servant or your debtor, and kill the snake.

key_terms.تَتَخَوَّفُهَا: you fear it or apprehend danger from it
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory salat (prayer), as opposed to a voluntary prayer
key_terms.غَرِيمًا: a debtor or one involved in a financial claim
key_terms.غُلَامًا: a servant or slave in one’s possession

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to break an obligatory salat (prayer) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that an obligatory salat (prayer) may be interrupted when an urgent harm or significant worldly right requires immediate action. It shows that preserving oneself, recovering a runaway servant, pursuing a debtor, and removing direct danger like a snake can take precedence over continuing the prayer.
